attractions.name: Badshahi Mosque
attractions.description: A 17th-century Mughal-era mosque, one of the largest in the world, known for its red sandstone architecture and marble domes.

attractions.name: Lahore Fort (Shahi Qila)
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage citadel showcasing Mughal architecture, including the Sheesh Mahal and Alamgiri Gate.

attractions.name: Shalimar Gardens
attractions.description: A Mughal-era terraced garden with fountains and reflecting pools, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

attractions.name: Minar-e-Pakistan
attractions.description: A national monument in Iqbal Park marking the site of the 1940 Lahore Resolution.

attractions.name: Lahore Museum
attractions.description: One of Pakistan's oldest and largest museums, housing Mughal, Sikh, and colonial-era artifacts.

attractions.name: Anarkali Bazaar
attractions.description: One of the oldest surviving markets in South Asia, known for clothing, handicrafts, and street food.

attractions.name: Wagah Border Flag Ceremony
attractions.description: A daily military ceremony at the Pakistan-India border, popular for its patriotic atmosphere.

travel_tips.tip: Use the Lahore Ring Road to bypass the congested city center when traveling between the airport, Gulberg, and the Walled City area.
The Orange Line Metro Train and Metrobus are the cheapest ways to move between major landmarks; ride-hailing apps are best for door-to-door convenience.
Keep valuables secure in crowded areas like Anarkali Bazaar and the Walled City, especially during peak shopping hours.
Visit the Walled City (Badshahi Mosque, Lahore Fort) early morning or late afternoon to avoid midday heat and crowds; arrive at Wagah Border by 4-4:30pm for the evening ceremony.

history.founded: Ancient city with references going back over 2,000 years
history.city_history: Lahore has been a major cultural and political center for centuries, serving as a capital under the Ghaznavids, the Delhi Sultanate, and most famously the Mughal Empire, who left behind the Lahore Fort, Badshahi Mosque, and Shalimar Gardens. It later became a key city of the Sikh Empire under Ranjit Singh, then the capital of British Punjab, and today remains Pakistan's cultural capital.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
